### Original Notes:
#### The Wish:
"I wish for Malm, Deyrale and Kix to retain their original sense of self, and to have eternal life."

Sense of Self:

- All memories and moral beliefs are preserved forever. Personality, relationships, and opinions are freely open to change.

Eternal Life can be a curse.

Kix lunges towards Lord Gallium with a disintegrate spell in his chest. Both of them disappear. Lord Gallium's Ulathrid state is dead, and Kix's body is gone.

Kix is now in an extradimensional sphere, somewhere in the nine hells. For him to be released, he must be found.
![](data:image/png;base64,)

As for Malm and Deyrale:

Malm has been crushed under a stone for some years. He has been felt a range of pain throughout this time, as he has faded in and out of consciousness. A normal Plasmoid would be dead.

Deyrale has spent some years in the nine hells. He has been stabbed, slashed, tortured, bruised, and beat beyond death. However, he still lives without a scratch.


### Immortality rules in actual play:

Because Deyrale and Malm are player characters, there will be some rules regarding the gameplay of their immortality.

If Deyrale or Malm are brought to 0hp, they will begin rolling death saving throws. However, it is not focused on three successes or failures, its focused on the following:
- **The focus is on failures and natural 20s.** The player may roll in the attempts of reaching a natural 20. However, they will keep track of their failures, and each failure after hitting 3 failed death saving throws will give the character a level of exhaustion once they wake up.
- For example, if Deyrale gets downed and rolls 5 failed death saving throws, whenever he wakes up next he will have **2 levels of exhaustion.** If his next roll is a natural 20, he wakes up immediately with 1 hp, and 2 levels of exhaustion.
- If a character rolls **8 failed death saving throws,** they are no longer allowed to keep rolling death saves. Instead of waking up after a short rest, they will wake up after a long rest with 4 levels of exhaustion.
- If a character is hit with **double their maximum damage threshold,** which typically results in instant death, they will begin rolling with 3 failed death saving throws.
